newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares down, milling stocks still tops.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares down, milling stocks still tops.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell slightly on Tuesday in moderate trade that continued to be dominated by popular milling stocks, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index was down 0.07 points to 234.87 while turnover was an average 24.04 million pounds ($7.07 million).
"Activity was back to normal today, most of it was in the milling shares, where profit is guaranteed," said broker Maher Fahmi.
The exchange came to a complete standstill on Sunday after the bourse computer system crashed and was restored five minutes before the end of the session.
Technical problems from a new dealing system hindered trade on the bourse on Monday but about 70 percent of that day's turnover came from trade of milling shares.
The popular firms were still top of the exchange on Tuesday but most of their share prices ended lower or unchanged.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills lead the way, after trade in more than 3.40 million pounds but the stock ended 0.65 pounds lower at 52.35.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the only milling stock that increased in value, ending 1.20 pounds higher at 48.50 after trade in more than three million pounds.
East Delta Flour Mills was down 0.75 pounds to 36.50. Central Egypt Flour Mills fell 0.37 to finish at 27.52 pounds.
Arab Cotton Ginning ended unchanged at 35.00 pounds after trade in more than 1.4 million pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell 1.12 points to 359.02 while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose 0.23 points to 163.62.
